findings.statement: NVIDIA offers system‑level data‑center offerings under the DGX platform.
NVIDIA's data‑center portfolio comprises accelerated compute, systems, networking, and software.
NVIDIA currently sells AI computing and data‑center platforms in the United States and Europe, with no new markets identified yet.
The internal company profile does not specify any planned NVIDIA product or service for launch.
Capacity constraints for NVIDIA deployments include available accelerator supply, qualified system configurations, deployment lead time, and serviceable capacity.

Broadcom supplies AI accelerators (custom ASICs such as TPUs and XPUs) and data‑center platform components (Tomahawk Ethernet switches, Jericho fabric solutions, high‑speed SerDes, and co‑packaged optics) to customers in both the United States and Europe.

Broadcom lists a public list price of $13,000 per TPU ASIC chip and $5,000 per other custom ASIC chip; the pricing is expressed as a per‑chip list price rather than a subscription or usage‑based model.

Broadcom bundles its AI accelerators (XPUs/TPUs) with networking hardware (Tomahawk and Jericho Ethernet switches, NICs, PCIe components, integrated optics) and adds software services such as the AI Services tile and support contracts, delivering end‑to‑end AI infrastructure solutions marketed for deployments in the United States and Europe.

Intel Corp: Intel provides AI accelerators and data‑center GPUs for AI workloads in both Europe and the United States. The Gaudi 3 AI accelerator is offered through IBM Cloud in the Frankfurt (eu‑de) region and the Washington, D.C. (us‑east) region, with a planned rollout to Dallas (us‑south) in Q2 2025. Intel also markets the Data Center GPU Flex Series and Data Center GPU Max Series for AI inference, analytics and rendering workloads.

Intel Corp: Intel bundles a software suite called the Intel® AI Software Bundle with qualifying hardware purchases. The bundle includes premium software (e.g., Adobe Creative Cloud Pro, Adobe Express) and featured AI‑related tools (e.g., AI Playground, Iterate.ai® Generate for AI PC, Render FX™ by Distinct AI) whose listed retail values are disclosed, representing a packaged offering of software with Intel AI hardware.

Intel Corp: On May 19 2025 Intel announced the launch of the Gaudi 3 AI accelerator (available in PCIe CEM and rack‑scale form factors) and an extension of the Intel Arc Pro GPU lineup for prosumers and AI developers. The Gaudi 3 accelerators were made available on IBM Cloud in Frankfurt (EU) and Washington, D.C. (US) at launch, with a planned addition of the Dallas (US) region in Q2 2025.

Broadcom’s AI accelerator customers may obtain hardware via lease or deferred‑payment arrangements rather than outright purchase; the company’s filings note leasing of custom AI accelerators (XPUs) and full AI racks, and alternative financing through its AI XPV platform, indicating a flexible pricing model beyond list‑price chip sales.

Broadcom embeds AI services into VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) 9.0, creating an AI‑native platform that bundles GPU monitoring, model store, model runtime, agent builder, vector database, and data indexing services as part of the VCF subscription, with the AI services slated for availability in Q1 FY26 for customers in the United States and Europe.

In February 2026 Broadcom announced the industry’s first enterprise Wi‑Fi 8 access‑point and switch solution for the AI era, featuring the BCM49438 APU with Wi‑Fi 8 radio chips and the Trident X3+ BCM56390 switch; the solution entered a sampling phase with early‑access customers and partners in the United States and Europe.

Intel Corp: Intel’s AI PC Acceleration Program bundles the upcoming Intel® Core Ultra processors with a software ecosystem, co‑engineering resources, design assistance, and co‑marketing support for ISVs and hardware partners, providing an integrated hardware‑software package for AI‑enabled PCs.

Intel Corp: Intel’s “Software AI Accelerators” are provided free of charge, delivering 10‑100× performance gains on existing CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs or dedicated accelerators without additional hardware costs or subscription fees.

Presence in the target markets: compared with NVIDIA Corporation, Broadcom is comparable. Broadcom supplies AI accelerators and data‑center networking components to customers in both the United States and Europe, confirming its market presence comparable to NVIDIA.

Presence in the target markets: compared with NVIDIA Corporation, Intel Corp is comparable. Intel’s Gaudi 3 accelerator and Data Center GPUs are available on IBM Cloud in Frankfurt and Washington, D.C., with further U.S. rollout planned, indicating a presence comparable to NVIDIA in the United States and Europe.

Offering and localisation for those markets: compared with NVIDIA Corporation, Broadcom is comparable. Broadcom offers custom ASIC AI accelerators (TPU, XPU) together with Tomahawk/Jericho networking hardware and an AI Services software tile, bundled into VMware Cloud Foundation for AI workloads in the United States and Europe, matching NVIDIA’s AI hardware‑software platform approach.

Offering and localisation for those markets: compared with NVIDIA Corporation, Intel Corp is comparable. Intel provides the Gaudi 3 AI accelerator, Data Center GPU Flex/Max series, and the Intel® AI Software Bundle, with deployments on IBM Cloud in Europe and the United States and bundled software support, offering a comparable AI hardware‑software portfolio to NVIDIA.

Target customers and positioning: compared with NVIDIA Corporation, Broadcom is comparable. Broadcom’s bundled AI accelerator and networking solutions, integrated into VMware Cloud Foundation, are aimed at enterprise data‑center operators and cloud providers, aligning with NVIDIA’s focus on CSPs and AI developers.

Target customers and positioning: compared with NVIDIA Corporation, Intel Corp is comparable. Intel’s Gaudi 3 deployment on IBM Cloud and its Data Center GPUs, together with the AI Software Bundle and AI PC Acceleration Program, are positioned for cloud service providers, AI developers, and OEM partners, mirroring NVIDIA’s primary customer segments.

Partnerships and distribution: compared with NVIDIA Corporation, Broadcom is comparable. Broadcom partners with VMware, embedding AI services into VMware Cloud Foundation, and works with early‑access customers for its Wi‑Fi 8 solution, reflecting a partnership model similar to NVIDIA’s ecosystem approach.

Partnerships and distribution: compared with NVIDIA Corporation, Intel Corp is comparable. Intel partners with IBM Cloud for Gaudi 3 availability and runs an AI PC Acceleration Program with OEMs and ISVs, providing distribution channels comparable to NVIDIA’s partner‑centric strategy.

U.S. export control rules currently omit chips-as-a-service, allowing Chinese companies to benefit from advanced AI chips via cloud while the hardware stays on U.S. soil, highlighting a regulatory gap in AI export controls for cloud-based services.

Brokers are providing anonymous overseas computing power that enables Chinese engineers to access banned Nvidia AI chips, indicating active demand and circumvention mechanisms despite export restrictions.
IndiaAI Compute provides powerful GPUs at significantly lower costs, ensuring GPU accelerator availability for AI developers in India.
Intel's GPU market share is reported as zero percent, showing negligible presence in the AI computing platform market.
Azure offers per‑second billing for compute capacity with no long‑term commitments, enabling flexible consumption for AI workloads.
Azure Reserved Virtual Machine Instances provide significant cost reductions compared to pay‑as‑you‑go rates when customers commit to one‑year or three‑year terms, useful for stable AI workloads.
Alibaba Cloud offers a dedicated Machine Learning Platform for AI with its own pricing page, indicating AI‑compute services are available in the Asian market.
India is building a comprehensive AI compute ecosystem, which supports rapid adoption of NVIDIA's AI platforms by fostering local research institutions and developer communities.
IndiaAI Compute provides powerful GPUs at significantly lower costs to academia, startups, and industry, indicating strong GPU accelerator availability and demand growth in the Indian market.
NVIDIA offers free cloud credits through its partners in India, demonstrating an active cloud partner network that facilitates scalable AI development and deployment.
Intel's GPU market share is effectively zero, indicating minimal competition from Intel in AI computing platforms.
South Korea's AI data center market is projected to grow from $0.58 billion in 2025 to $1.89 billion by 2030, a 26.61% CAGR, showing strong demand growth for AI computing platforms.
